streaming_input.text: Common causes include too much load, blocked cooling airflow, power-supply trouble,
or mechanical drag from worn bearings or rubbing parts. Frequent starts, long runs
, a hot room, and internal electrical damage can also create excess heat, but
those categories alone cannot identify what is wrong with your motor.
Keep it off; disconnect every energy source, prevent restart, control stored energy,
and allow cooling. Review whether heat followed clogging, longer runs, repeated starts
, or electrical work; inspect externally for blocked vents or damage. If permitted,
hand-turn the mechanism for drag. Clues aren't conclusive: trips or burning
odor need a technician; smoke or flames mean leave and call emergency services.
